title: Find Anything
tagline: Type part of a name, get the file, from every drive, in a blink.
what: A file search that the AI assistants on my Linux PC can ask: part of a name, a file type, a size or a date. It answers from an index of my drives instead of searching them file by file.
built: Taught it the search language of the Everything search tool: wildcards, file type, size, dates and text inside files
Hooked it to FSearch's index of over 6 million files, so sizes and dates come back without touching the disk
Pointed it at my home folder, every local drive, Google Drive and my home server's shared folders
Finding the video files over 40 GB in my media library takes 0.06 seconds
credit: I wrote the search; FSearch, plocate, fd and ripgrep do the indexing and the digging.
starring: My AI chats, any time they need to find a file

making.problem: When I moved to Linux, my AI assistants needed the same whole-machine file search they'd used on Windows.
how: It takes the question in Everything's own search language.
It looks the answer up in FSearch's file index first, and in plocate's for the system folders FSearch skips. Both are free indexing tools.
Only for 'changed today' questions, which the indexes haven't caught up on, does it walk the disk live.
Questions about the text inside files go to ripgrep, a fast text search.

moment.what: I ask for the video files over 40 GB in my media library. The answer comes back in 0.06 seconds, from the index, without walking the drives.
